g.text: do / the Planner or the Owner writes the issue
do / cumin waits for a free slot
do / GitHub runs the required checks
do / the Reviewer reviews the pull request
do / the Owner reviews the pull request
do / cumin merges the pull request,
[the Owner added ready, the blockers are closed,
/ cumin requests a check fix from the Implementer
asked a question, or it is the second time]
/ cumin requests the review from the Reviewer
[no Reviewer runs, and: the Implementer or the Owner
moved the head commit, or a check does not pass]
[a required check failed and the fix requests
are at the limit; or a check gave no result in time]
[no Reviewer runs, the Reviewer requested changes
on the head commit, the rounds are under the limit]
/ cumin requests a review fix from the Implementer
[no Reviewer runs, the Reviewer approved the
head commit, the checks passed, risk/low]
[no Reviewer runs, the Reviewer approved the
[no Reviewer runs, the Reviewer left no review
on the head commit, first time]
[no Reviewer runs, and: the rounds are at the limit,
the Reviewer asked a question, or it is the second time]
/ cumin requests a response from the Implementer
[GitHub shows the pull request as merged]
/ cumin closes the issue and writes
PROPOSAL. A box is a state: a label on GitHub (written without "cumin/status/").
"do /" says who works in the state. An arrow is: trigger [guard] / effect, each with its actor.
Every guard reads only facts on GitHub and "no agent runs for this issue".
No arrow needs the event "the run ended": a restart of cumin loses nothing.
"merging" makes a merge whose answer was lost visible: the next poll reads whether the pull request is merged.
